title: Simulation-based tryout: 72hr hire + on-board protocol
body:
Overview - why this pilot

We are piloting a 72-hour simulation-based tryout for mid-senior platform and inference engineers. The goal is to replace a portion of synchronous interview time with a bounded, realistic work simulation that surfaces collaboration patterns, production judgment, and ramp risk. This doc captures the candidate flow, scoring rubric, conversion criteria, and an immediate post-convert onboarding pack.

Primary goals
- Increase signal on real-day problem solving and cross-team collaboration
- Reduce interviewing scheduling overhead by shifting to asynchronous artifacts + one live touchpoint
- Improve ramp prediction by capturing evidence against concrete onboarding milestones

Hypothesis
- Candidates who complete a focused simulation project plus a short synchronous handoff will have 30% better first-90-day impact signal vs. traditional onsite loops (measured via mentor-rated ramp progress).

High level flow (72 hours)
1) Day 0: Offer simulation invite and set expectations (email + Slack DM). Package includes a short product context doc, dataset / repo stub, and three deliverables.
2) Day 1: Candidate completes Deliverable A - design note (1-2 pages) outlining approach, tradeoffs, and rollout plan. Encourage diagrams, rollout safety, fallback strategies.
3) Day 2: Candidate completes Deliverable B - implementation snapshot: a short PR or annotated pseudocode showing core change, plus unit tests or test plan. This can be in a repo created for the candidate.
4) Day 3: Candidate completes Deliverable C - async cross-team handoff: a 20-minute written handoff + a 30-minute live pairing/handoff call with 2 interviewers (team engineering lead + product).
5) Submission window closes at 72 hours. Interview panel collects artifacts and performs scoring within 48 hours of close.

Deliverables - guidance to candidate
- Keep the design note concise. Focus on safety, latency/cost implications, and metrics.
- Implementation snapshot should be runnable or demonstrable. If infra access is required, provide a lightweight local mock.
- Handoff should anticipate follow-ups and include a short acceptance test matrix.

Evaluation rubric (shared across interviewers) - scale 1-5 for each area
- Technical correctness and code hygiene (1-5) - correctness, modularity, tests, clarity of PR comments.
- Systems design & inferencing judgment (1-5) - tradeoffs, scaling, KV cache, batching decisions, fallback policies.
- Production thinking & safety (1-5) - observability hooks, rollback plan, cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Cross-team communication (1-5) - clarity in written design and handoff, anticipation of questions, async-first style.
- Learning velocity & curiosity (1-5) - iteration speed across deliverables, receptiveness in live call.
- Cultural and role fit (1-5) - ownership, collaboration, and signals for mentorability.

Scoring notes and thresholds
- Panel aggregates numeric scores and writes 2 short notes (strength, top risk).
- Passing threshold: average across categories >= 3.6 and no single critical area < 3. Critical areas for seniors: Systems design & Production thinking.
- Borderline cases escalate to hiring committee for calibration with evidence artifacts.

Conversion -> onboarding micro-pack (if offer accepted)
- 72hr convert pack to be delivered immediately on acceptance: access list, first-7-day mini-project, mentor pairing, prioritized docs.
- First-7-day mini-project: ship a small telemetry dashboard or a CLI health-check that exercises platform dev flow. Objective: produce a PR and a short demo.
- Mentor rotation: week 1 mentor is shadow + reviewer, week 2 rotates to on-call buddy, week 3 pairs on feature work.

Operational runbook (people-ops + hiring manager)
- Create candidate repo template and CI stub - owner: Eng Tools (ticket ENG-5276).
- Prep candidate context package - owner: hiring manager. Use 2-3 screenshots, perf numbers, dataset example.
- Scheduling: automate the 30-minute live handoff slot selection using Scheduler tool.
- Panel calibration meeting: hold a 1hr post-pilot review after first 10 hires to compare scores to first-30-day mentor ratings.

Artifacts to store per candidate
- Design note (PDF or markdown)
- PR / code snapshot (link to ephemeral repo)
- Handoff notes (markdown)
- Panel scoring sheet (one-line rationale per category)
- Mentor baseline rating at day 14 and day 30 (to evaluate ramp hypothesis)

Template scoring prompts for reviewers (copy into scoring sheet)
- What was the strongest technical signal from artifacts?
- What introduces the biggest ramp risk? (be specific: infra, domain, code quality)
- Would you assign this candidate a 1:1 mentor with 2 weeks of pairing? yes/no + why

Acceptance checklist for candidate-to-employee conversion (to be completed by hiring manager + onboarding ops)
- Confirm offer signed and start date set
- Provision accounts (git, CI, cloud) before day 1 - owner: IT ops
- Assign mentor and schedule week1 checkpoints - owner: hiring manager
- Create first-7-day mini-project ticket in team backlog - owner: tech lead

Pilot success metrics (30/60/90 day)
- Time-to-meaningful-PR: median days to first team-merged PR (target: <= 14 days)
- Mentor satisfaction: median mentor rating at day 30 (target: >= 4/5)
- Interview cost: reduction in synchronous interview hours per hire (target: 25% reduction)
- Candidate experience: NPS survey after tryout (target: >= +30)

To-dos and owners (short list)
- Build candidate repo template and example PR - Liam Chen - due 2025-11-20
- Draft candidate context package and test data - hiring managers (platform)- Priya Desai - due 2025-11-18
- Create Slack workflow for candidate invites - People Ops - Marina Okafor - due 2025-11-12
- Panel scoring sheet in Google Form and auto-aggregation - Omar Ruiz - due 2025-11-14

Open questions / risks
- Candidate fairness: we need accessible options for candidates who cannot do full-time 72hrs (offer split windows or pro-rated delivery).
- IP and repo hygiene: ephemeral repos must be squashed and wiped; legal signoff needed for work-submitted clauses. Legal contact: Erin Patel (legal).
- Evaluation bias: require at least 3 reviewers per candidate to reduce single-reviewer bias.

Notes to reviewers and interviewers
- Be explicit in the panel notes. Raw scores are useful but the 2 short supporting comments (strength, risk) carry the calibration weight.
- Use evidence links not memory: attach artifacts to the panel form.
- If a candidate submits less than 2 deliverables, flag as incomplete and follow the incomplete flow (call with candidate to resolve or close).

Appendix - quick templates
- Candidate invite subject line: Simulation tryout - Redwood Inference - 72 hr window
- Acceptable deliverable formats: md, pdf, git PR link, zip of code, demo recording link
- Live handoff agenda (30 min): 10 min candidate demo, 10 min clarifying Qs, 5 min follow-ups, 5 min panel notes

TL;DR
Run a bounded, evidence-rich 72hr simulation for targeted roles, score across six dimensions, convert passing candidates into a standardized micro-onboard pack. Pilot ownership: People Ops with Eng Tools and hiring managers. Draft -> please review and add calibration comments in the linked Confluence page.
